claims.explanation: Pyrimethamine selectively kills cancer cells that depend on de novo nucleotide biosynthesis, particularly through DHFR and thymidylate synthase (TYMS), while cells with high expression of folate transporters or low DHFR activity are less affected. The transcriptional similarity to methotrexate and raltitrexed supports a DHFR/TS-targeting mechanism. Additionally, squamous and mesenchymal lineages may be more sensitive due to higher proliferation and nucleotide demand.

features.basis: Target enzyme; higher expression may indicate dependency
Thymidylate synthase is a downstream target of antifolates; high expression may predict sensitivity
Reduced folate carrier; mediates uptake of antifolates
Polyglutamation of antifolates enhances retention and activity
One-carbon metabolism enzyme; upregulated in responsive lines (HCC515)
Most sensitive lines have TP53 mutations; loss of p53 may impair DNA repair and increase dependence on nucleotide synthesis
Common in sensitive lines; PI3K pathway activation may increase nucleotide demand
Loss of PTEN activates PI3K/AKT, potentially increasing nucleotide synthesis
KRAS mutations appear in several least-affected lines; may drive alternative nucleotide synthesis pathways
BRAF mutations in some resistant lines; may indicate lower dependency on DHFR
Drug efflux pump; high expression may reduce intracellular pyrimethamine
Annotated target; may mediate efflux or alter drug distribution
